title: Best Trading App in India (2026): Top 10 Apps Compared
summary: Compare the best trading apps in India by brokerage, F&O tools, charts, APIs and US investing access. Find the right app for your trading style.
body_markdown:
Choosing the best trading app in India is not only about brokerage. You also need reliable execution, useful charts, suitable market segments and an interface that matches how you trade.


Groww is easy for beginners, Zerodha offers a strong all-round experience and Dhan suits active options traders. Kotak Neo stands out for low F&O brokerage. Your best choice depends on how you trade.

*Brokerage excludes STT, GST, stamp duty, exchange fees, DP charges and other applicable costs. Charges and promotional plans can change, so verify the broker’s pricing page before opening an account.


This comparison focuses on pricing, trading tools, market access, usability and suitability for different types of traders. The list is not based on brokerage alone.


## 1. Zerodha Kite


Zerodha Kite is a strong all-round app. Its clean interface includes advanced charts, GTT orders, baskets, alerts and detailed reports through Console.


Equity delivery has zero brokerage. Equity intraday and futures cost ₹20 or 0.03% per executed order, whichever is lower, while options cost ₹20 per order. Its usability, tools and transparent Zerodha pricing suit traders who want a proven platform.


**Best for:** Traders looking for a balanced platform and established trading ecosystem.


## 2. Groww


Groww is one of the best trading apps for beginners. Stocks, mutual funds, IPOs and F&O are available in a simple interface, with charts, indicators and option-chain data.


Groww charges ₹20 or 0.1% per equity order, whichever is lower, subject to a ₹5 minimum. F&O orders generally cost ₹20. Check the latest details on the Groww pricing page.


**Best for:** Beginners who want investing and trading in one app.


## 3. Dhan


Dhan offers TradingView charts, basket orders, an advanced option chain and a separate Options Trader platform with pre-built strategies.


Equity delivery is brokerage-free. Intraday trades cost ₹20 or 0.03% per executed order, whichever is lower, while futures and options cost ₹20 per order under Dhan’s standard pricing.


**Best for:** F&O traders who need advanced charts and execution tools.

## 4. Upstox


Upstox combines investing with Chart 360, TradingView charts, more than 100 indicators, option-chain analytics and GTT orders.


Upstox charges up to ₹20 per executed order for stocks, F&O, commodities and currencies. Mutual funds and IPOs have zero commission. AMC and onboarding charges can depend on the account type and offer, as explained on the Upstox charges page.


**Best for:** Active traders who want feature-rich mobile and web charts.


## 5. Angel One


Angel One combines broking with research, screeners and portfolio tools across stocks, F&O, commodities, mutual funds and IPOs.


After the introductory offer, equity delivery and intraday brokerage is generally ₹20 or 0.1% per order, whichever is lower, with a ₹5 minimum. F&O costs ₹20 per executed order. Review the latest Angel One charges before signing up.


**Best for:** Traders and investors who value research and market insights.


## 6. Kotak Neo


Kotak Neo is worth considering if brokerage is your priority. Under its Trade Free Plan, equity intraday costs ₹10 or 0.05% per order, whichever is lower, and F&O costs ₹10 per order. Equity delivery is charged at 0.20% under this plan. Other plans have different rates.


Its wider banking ecosystem can help existing Kotak customers. Compare the current Kotak Neo pricing plans.


**Best for:** Active traders seeking lower F&O brokerage.


## 7. FYERS


FYERS focuses on charting, trading tools and API access. It is particularly relevant to technical traders and users who want to create custom trading workflows.


Equity intraday and futures cost ₹20 or 0.03% per order, whichever is lower. Options cost ₹20, while delivery costs ₹20 or 0.3% per order, whichever is lower. See the complete FYERS pricing.


**Best for:** Technical traders and API users.


## 8. 5paisa


5paisa offers stocks, derivatives and mutual funds through one platform. Its ₹20-per-order pricing is easy to understand, although frequent traders should compare total costs.


**Best for:** Users who prefer straightforward flat-fee pricing.


## 9. HDFC Sky


HDFC Sky brings stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, IPOs and derivatives into one app, which can suit existing HDFC customers.


Equity delivery and intraday orders cost ₹20 or 2.5% of transaction value, whichever is lower. Options cost ₹20 per order. Check HDFC Sky pricing for other segments and account charges.


**Best for:** HDFC customers and investors seeking an all-in-one app.


## 10. ICICI Direct


ICICI Direct combines trading with research, investment products and banking integration.


Its brokerage depends on the selected plan. Compare delivery, derivatives, subscription and MTF costs on its brokerage page.


**Best for:** ICICI customers and investors who value research and banking convenience.


## Which Trading App Is Best for You?


-


**For beginners:** Groww offers the simplest starting experience.


-


**For overall usability:** Zerodha Kite provides a balanced set of tools.


-


**For**[options trading:](https://algotest.in/blog/options-trading-a-comprehensive-guide-with-algorithmic-strategies) Dhan offers dedicated F&O features.


-


**For lower F&O brokerage:** Kotak Neo is competitively priced under eligible plans.


-


**For technical traders:** FYERS and Upstox provide strong charting tools.


-


**For bank-backed convenience:** Consider HDFC Sky or ICICI Direct.


Before deciding, compare reliability, order types, brokerage, AMC, DP charges, API costs and customer support. The cheapest app is not automatically the best trading app for your workflow.


## What to Check Before Choosing a Trading App


### Total trading cost


Look beyond the advertised brokerage. AMC, DP charges on share sales, call-and-trade fees, MTF interest, API subscriptions and platform plans can change your actual cost.


### Trading tools and reliability


Active traders should compare chart quality, option-chain data, order types, basket orders and execution stability. Investors may care more about research, portfolio reports, IPOs and mutual funds.


### API and algo trading support


If you plan to automate later, check whether the broker offers stable API access and integrates with your preferred platform. This guide to the[best brokers for algo trading in India](https://algotest.in/blog/best-brokers-for-algo-trading-in-india/) compares API access, costs and trading support.


## What About Apps for Investing in US Stocks?


Most apps in this list focus mainly on Indian markets. If you want to invest in US stocks, compare the access route separately. Indian investors may use a GIFT City platform or an international investing partner, depending on the provider.


Check currency-conversion and remittance costs, available stocks and ETFs, fractional investing, custody, withdrawals and applicable Indian tax rules.
